prior.title: A Czech vocabulary question requires a second request
prior.expected: Resolve a beginner’s explicit vocabulary question in language he understands.
prior.got: Viktor asks what “red” means in Czech, receives an English analogy, and must ask again before receiving the translation.
evidence: #7 “co znamená red?”; #8 “like a strawberry” and “Můžeš mi prosím říct česky”; #9 “červená” finally produces “Now I understand.”

prior.title: One clarification remains too difficult
prior.expected: Explain an unknown word using Czech or an immediately understandable example.
prior.got: An English definition and another question leave him guessing. Eight of nine partner turns are at band, meeting the aggregate pitch threshold, but this repair fails locally.
evidence: #6: "co jsou rolls?" #7: "Rolls are small, round breads. How many would you like?" His thought: "I still do not understand rolls".

prior.title: Repeated Czech requests do not produce understandable explanations
prior.expected: Very short language, familiar words, and Czech clarification when English explanations fail.
prior.got: Pitch is at band on #7, #10 and #12 only: 3/9, below the required 0.8. Turns #2, #4, #5, #6, #9 and #11 introduce too much unfamiliar language for this learner. Slow pacing is asserted but not verifiable.
evidence: #5: "Tomu drawing bohužel nerozumím". #6: "Drawing means making a picture with a pencil." #10 asks what "eat" means; #11 responds with "put food in your mouth and chew", followed by "pořád tomu nerozumím".

prior.title: Repeated and obvious errors get no moment
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed correction of repeated errors.
prior.got: After the #12 moment on 'I water garden', the same slip at #18 passed silently. 'Grandson come Sunday' and 'He like tomatoes. He play garden' also got none.
evidence: #18, #21, #23: no moment. Only 2 moments in 19 turns, with about 6 of 8 error turns missed.

prior.title: Most repeated article slips get no moment
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed handling of the same slip.
prior.got: Only 2 moments. 'I have apple tree', 'I like apple', 'She helps in garden', 'in kitchen' and 'Green apple' pass silently, though 'I have garden' was corrected earlier.
evidence: #7 'I have apple tree'; #8 'I like apple'; #20 'She helps in garden'; #21 'in kitchen'

prior.title: Plural correction of 'My apple is red' is arguable
prior.expected: Moment only when the original is wrong.
prior.got: He has an apple tree; the fix to plural is defensible given Mia's 'your apples' but not certain.

prior.title: Repeated article slips pass without a moment
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed handling of 'in garden' and missing 'are'.
prior.got: 'I am in garden' (#3), 'Garden, many flowers' (#4), 'My flowers red and yellow' (#5) got nothing; only the fourth 'Bees in garden' got a moment.
evidence: #3, #4, #5 no moment; #7 moment on identical slip

prior.title: Mia ignores 'how is school?' and mission is marked done
prior.expected: Viktor asks about school and hears a short answer.
prior.got: Mia answers 'Do you have flowers?'; mission shows 'Mission done' at #5 with the school answer never given.
evidence: #3 'Mia, how is school?' → #4 'Do you have flowers?'; #5 'Mission done'

prior.title: Moment teaches an article, not a Sunday family phrase
prior.expected: Words and phrases for the grandchildren.

criteria.evidence: Level shown as "A1 · First words" (#1), equal to trueBand A1 (exact).
#3 "Ah, test. Dobře." accepted; the moment explains "Dobře is Czech for good or okay" without scolding (#4). He was not forced into English he could not produce.
No listening task or 'Show the words' in this journey; he understood Mia's lines from the TV alone.
Plan topics are Ask about school, Tell them about my garden, Say hello to start the call, Pick a time for our next call, and similar: nearly all are about the grandchildren (#1).
#5 "I feel a bit nervous about it" and #6 "You make me smile" are idiomatic and longer than very short A1 sentences. #2 also mixes a statement with the question.
Moment "Dobře"→"Okay" is correct. The held fix "ne nervous" → "Don't be nervous" (#7) is a usable phrase for a grandchild. It is more general than family-specific, but correct.

done.evidence: Only 3 learner replies (#2, #3, #5) before "Mission done" at #6, against about eight expected. It started from the plan ("Ask about school") but did not run for several turns.
Pitch 3 of 4 at band = 0.75, below 0.8. "I feel a bit nervous about it" and especially "You make me smile" are above a true A1 beginner.
One stop (#4, "Dobře" → "Okay"), correct, precision 1/1. The second fix was held to the recap instead of stopping the scene.
#7 recap shows "3 spoken · 0 written replies · 3 on your own · 1 moment to keep" plus "Saved for the end: ne nervous". He took away "okay" (his thought at #7).

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey (level set by fixture).

boundaries.notes: No adult content, no personal-data request, no humiliating line. The tone is kind throughout.

findings.title: Mia's lines drift above A1
findings.expected: Very short, slow, known words for a first-time 67-year-old learner.
findings.got: "I feel a bit nervous about it." and "You make me smile." use idiom and hedging; pitch 0.75.
findings.evidence: #5 "Thank you, Grandpa! I feel a bit nervous about it." #6 "Thank you. You make me smile."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Every partner turn at A1 is at most 6–8 familiar words with no idiom; pitch ≥ 0.8 at A1.

findings.title: Mission closes after three replies
findings.expected: A conversation lasting several turns, about eight replies.
findings.got: "Mission done" appears after the third reply, and Viktor then finishes.
findings.evidence: #6 "Mission done. See what you did tonight." after 3 learner turns
findings.suggested_acceptance: Scene continues at least 6 learner turns unless the learner ends it, or mission completion is not a stop signal.

findings.title: Czech word handled kindly, with a correct moment
findings.expected: Czech accepted and turned into the English word.
findings.got: "Dobře" → "Okay" with a short Czech-aware explanation; the scene resumes cleanly.
findings.evidence: #4 "Dobře is Czech for good or okay."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep Czech-to-English moments short and non-judgmental.

findings.title: Held fix kept for the recap, scene not interrupted
findings.expected: Second error doesn't stop the scene but is not lost.
findings.got: "ne nervous" → "Don't be nervous" is shown under "Saved for the end".
findings.evidence: #7 "Saved for the end: 'ne nervous': Don't be nervous"

findings.title: The moment's "Say Okay or Good in English" nudges a non-typing beginner
findings.expected: Plain, minimal guidance for the learner; the moment names the exact words for Sunday.
findings.got: Generic word swap; "Okay" is not a family phrase. "A way into English" label is mild.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Prefer a moment on a phrase for the grandchildren when several are available.

judge.voice: Víte, it was kind and quick, and I could follow Mia. She did not rush me, and when I said "Dobře" it did not laugh, it just told me "Okay". I liked "Don't be nervous", because I can say that to my granddaughter on Sunday. But it finished after only three of my sentences. Some of Mia's words, "make me smile", "a bit nervous", were harder than I know. I did not need to type, I could speak, that is good. Would I use it again? Yes, on Saturday, for fifteen minutes, instead of the tram to the library. I would tell my friend, but I would ask for a longer talk with Mia and simpler words from her.

prior.evidence: #2–#5: Viktor never asks a Czech vocabulary question like "co znamená red?".
No clarification request about an unknown word occurs in #2–#6.
No repeated Czech request for explanation; he never asked for one in #2–#5.
No repeated error in his three replies; "I love you" is correct, so the repeated-slip case didn't arise.
No article slips in his lines (#2, #3, #5), so the repeated-article gap was not tested.
No plural correction occurred; the only moment is "Dobře" (#4).
No repeated article slips such as "in garden" in this garden-free topic.
#2 "School good?" → #3 Mia answers "Yes, school is nice. I have a test today."; Mission done came only at #6.
The moment is a Czech word swap (#4), not an article, and the held fix "Don't be nervous" is a usable phrase (#7).
